target.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics
target.body:
Fixes #95279

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Inbound user turns that OpenClaw decorates with model-facing metadata, plus the transcript readers that later render, replay, index, dedupe, or summarize those turns: Control UI chat text, CLI imported-session history, memory-host session corpus, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The root cause was a missing trusted source-of-truth contract for decorated inbound bodies: host-generated inbound metadata and user-authored text were stored in the same `content` string, so downstream consumers had to parse forgeable plaintext sentinels such as `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` or `Sender (untrusted metadata):`. Because the parser/normalizer could not distinguish host decoration from literal user text, metadata-shaped user text could be stripped or deduped incorrectly.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who paste or type metadata-looking text should not lose that text from chat history, imported-history dedupe, session logs, memory export, or historical replay when OpenClaw has a trusted bare body for the inbound turn.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix for a compatibility-sensitive session-state and data-format contract bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:** This PR adds an additive trusted inbound contract: persisted/runtime user messages can carry `inboundDecorated: true` plus `bareBody`, and inbound template context can carry `InboundDecorated` plus `BareBody`. Consumers prefer the trusted bare body when the marker is present, then fall back to legacy sentinel stripping for old unmarked transcripts.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This fixes the source contract instead of adding another sentinel parser. The resolver treats `bareBody` as authoritative only when the trusted inbound marker is present, and the updated readers share that resolver so display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage logs all map decorated messages from the same non-forgeable contract rather than independently parsing user-controlled text.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The source of truth is the trusted inbound metadata on the message or inbound context, not sentinel text in `content`. Active-turn model prompts may still contain inbound metadata; historical display, replay, indexing, dedupe, memory, and usage-log readers consume the trusted bare body when present.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** Scope boundary: this PR only adds and consumes the trusted inbound bare-body contract. It does not change active-turn prompt construction, does not remove legacy stripping for already-persisted rows, does not migrate transcript files, does not redesign plugin SDKs, and does not add unrelated provider/channel routing behavior.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** Existing unmarked transcripts keep their current legacy fallback. Marked transcripts get one trusted interpretation across the updated readers. The proof now includes both focused regression tests and an exact-head terminal runtime proof that imports the real reader functions and exercises a temp session transcript; external channel/gateway proof remains unavailable in this local environment and is disclosed below.
- **Risk labels considered:** `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** Consumers now trust `bareBody` only when `inboundDecorated === true` or `InboundDecorated === true`. A redaction hook that rewrites user `content` drops the prior trusted fields unless the hook explicitly supplies fresh trusted fields, preventing redacted content from being bypassed by stale bare-body metadata.
- **Why acceptable:** The contract is optional and backward-compatible. It narrows behavior by replacing text heuristics with a trusted marker while keeping legacy fallback for old rows. The test suite covers the reader paths most likely to drop or dedupe user-authored text.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Preserve literal inbound-metadata-looking user text through UI display/extraction, CLI import dedupe, memory-host export, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs when a decorated inbound turn carries a trusted bare body.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** Old transcripts without the trusted marker still use `stripInboundMetadata()` and related legacy cleanup, so existing stored sessions remain readable and do not need migration.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** External live gateway/channel proof remains unavailable in this local Windows/Git Bash environment because the prework check reports no local gateway proof capability for the reviewer-requested live channel run. The submitted proof is current-head repository runtime proof plus regression proof over transcript/UI/CLI/runtime/memory/session-log boundaries using a real temp session transcript and synthetic message data. Earlier broader checks also noted SonarLint was unavailable, `pnpm check:changed` was blocked by a launcher sanity check, and a full non-incremental `tsc` run exhausted local Node heap; focused Vitest, tsgo, oxlint, diff checks, and the exact-head runtime proof listed below passed in the repaired worktree.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Local Windows/Git Bash worktree, existing PR repair flow, repository Vitest runner, repository tsgo and oxlint runners from earlier repair rounds, and daily-fix verification bound to the current synced repair head `038b79c5afe04ca96a21b7af17b3f54732efbe5d`.
- **Commands run after this patch:** `git diff --check`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`; `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with an inline exact-head real behavior proof importing `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage`. Earlier repair rounds also passed the focused trusted-inbound suite, core tsgo, core-test tsgo, and oxlint shards after sync and conflict repair.
- **Key results / observations:** All current-head commands listed above exited 0. The new session usage log regression proves both compatibility paths: an unmarked decorated legacy row strips injected metadata to `hello there`, while a marked decorated row preserves a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from trusted `bareBody`. The exact-head runtime proof ran on `038b79c5afe04ca96a21b7af17b3f54732efbe5d`, wrote a temporary JSONL session transcript, imported the real `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage` functions, and observed: usage logs legacy row `hello there`; usage logs trusted row `"Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text, not injected metadata"`; memory corpus contains `"User: Conversation info (untrusted metadata): this is literal user text, not injected metadata"`; memory corpus omits the transport-decorated copy; UI normalization returns the trusted literal body. After syncing the repair branch onto current main to clear the remote merge conflict, `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` reported only two newer main commits, `sync_main_required=false`, `has_conflicts=false`, and no overlap files, so no further rebase is needed.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001 and RF-002 are addressed to the extent available in this contributor environment by the dedicated current-head real behavior proof below. RF-003 and RF-005 are explicitly maintainer-decision items: this PR proposes the trusted inbound contract as top-level `inboundDecorated` plus `bareBody` fields, and maintainers should accept or redirect that contract shape before merge. RF-004 is disclosed as the remaining external live gateway/channel gap because the local proof prework reports no gateway proof capability here. RF-006 was already a non-blocking maintainer pass signal.
- **Regression guardrail:** Target test file: `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`, with the focused regression added for the session usage log reader. Scenario locked in: one unmarked legacy decorated user row must still strip injected metadata, while one trusted decorated user row must preserve a literal `Conversation info (untrusted metadata):` string from `bareBody`. Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it exercises the exact consumer that ClawSweeper flagged and proves both the new trusted contract and the required legacy fallback. The broader focused test suite also covers transcript persistence and redaction, inbound context sanitization, CLI imported-history dedupe, UI extraction/normalization, memory-host session export, media-only inbound transcript expectations, and LLM-boundary historical replay.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings were reviewed. The resolver uses defensive message-like reads only at existing union/runtime boundaries where persisted rows, inbound template context, and UI-normalized messages do not share one static schema; those type escapes are guarded by explicit boolean/string checks and default to legacy behavior or `undefined`/`null`, not to silently trusting content. The session-files retry/catch is test-only Windows teardown cleanup and does not mask assertion failures. Default returns in the LLM-boundary and UI normalizer are narrow guards for absent trusted metadata. The larger diff is intentional because the contract must be written once and consumed at every affected display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log boundary; the latest merge-conflict resolution preserves current-main sender metadata under `__openclaw` while also preserving this PR's `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` fields.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local code paths covered by regression proof and current-head runtime proof. The only remaining caveat is the disclosed external live gateway/channel proof gap in this environment.

## Real behavior proof

- **Current-head redacted runtime transcript:** This PR now includes a current-head real behavior proof run on `038b79c5afe04ca96a21b7af17b3f54732efbe5d`. The proof was run outside Vitest with `node --import tsx --input-type=module`; it wrote a temporary session JSONL transcript, imported the repository's real reader functions, and executed `loadSessionLogs`, `buildSessionEntry`, and `normalizeMessage` against that transcript.

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
038b79c5afe04ca96a21b7af17b3f54732efbe5d

$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <inline exact-head runtime proof>
Exact-head runtime proof: PASS
HEAD: 038b79c5afe04ca96a21b7af17b3f54732efbe5d
usage logs legacy row: hello there
usage logs trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text, not injected metadata"
memory corpus trusted row: "User: Conversation info (untrusted metadata): this is literal user text, not injected metadata"
memory corpus omits decorated transport copy: true
UI normalized trusted row: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nthis is literal user text, not injected metadata"
EXIT_CODE=0
```

- **What this proves beyond tests:** The runtime proof exercises the same real reader functions that production reader paths use after transcript persistence: session usage logs strip legacy injected metadata, trusted decorated session rows preserve literal metadata-looking user text, memory-host indexing uses the trusted bare body instead of the decorated transport copy, and UI normalization returns the trusted literal body.
- **Boundary of this proof:** This is a local session-reader runtime proof from the repaired worktree, not a live external gateway/channel proof. The local environment could not provide the requested gateway/channel proof capability, so that gap remains disclosed for maintainer or ClawSweeper judgment.

## Implementation summary

- Add optional trusted inbound fields on persisted/runtime user messages and inbound template context.
- Persist the trusted bare body for decorated user turns while treating `before_message_write` as the redaction boundary.
- Update UI display, UI text extraction/search/export, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session indexing, LLM historical replay, and session usage logs to prefer the trusted bare body before legacy sentinel stripping.
- Keep legacy sentinel stripping for old transcripts that do not carry trusted fields.

## Scope boundary

In scope: inbound user-turn contract/type plumbing, transcript persistence/runtime merge preservation, UI display normalization, CLI imported-session dedupe, memory-host session export/indexing, LLM historical replay normalization, session usage logs, and regression tests for those paths.

Out of scope: transcript migration, removal of legacy fallback, active-turn model prompt construction changes, unrelated provider/channel routing, or broad plugin SDK redesign.

## Related PR scan

The daily-fix related open PR scan found related PR #94419 as advisory background only. This PR does not depend on that work and keeps the fix scoped to the trusted inbound bare-body contract requested by #95279.

## Verification history

Additional local validation from earlier repair rounds also passed after sync/rebase repair:

```text
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit=0

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-extract.test.ts ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.test.ts
# exit=0

node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8
# exit=0
```

## Merge risk

- Risk labels considered: `message-delivery`, `security-boundary`, `session-state`.
- Risk explanation: This changes display/replay/indexing/dedupe/log behavior for messages that explicitly opt into the trusted decorated contract. The security boundary is the trusted marker plus redaction-hook clearing behavior. Session-state risk is additive because old rows retain legacy sentinel stripping.
- Why acceptable: The contract is optional and backward-compatible, and the tests cover the affected boundaries.
